title: Binary Search
summary: You get a list `nums` of distinct integers sorted in increasing order and a number `target`. Return the position of `target` in `nums`, or -1 when it is not there, in logarithmic time.
constraints: the values in nums are distinct

approaches.twist: Compare the middle with the target and discard half.
Check every position from left to right.
approaches.note: Works, but a scan takes O(n) time. The target is O(log n).

signals.meaning: One look at the middle tells you which half to drop.
O(log n) means halving the range at every step.

constraintReading: The logarithmic time target rules out scanning the list, which is O(n).

hints.clarify: What should you return when the target is missing? Try target 5 in [2, 6, 7] by hand.
hints.approach: Keep a range lo..hi that could still hold the target. Look at the middle: it is the answer, or it tells you which half to drop.
hints.whyNot: A hash map needs O(n) time just to build it.

slots.setup: lo at 0, hi at the last index.
slots.update: Move lo past the middle when the middle is too small; move hi below it when it is too big.
slots.record: When the middle equals the target, return its index.
slots.return: If the range becomes empty, return -1.

solution.explanation: The range halves every step, so the time is O(log n). Only three integers are stored, so the space is O(1).

events.label: return
events.say: The range is empty: {target} is not there

predict.ask: Which index will mid point to next?

related.relation: Also two indexes moving toward each other, one step at a time instead of by halves.
